name: Process capital calls from general partners
summary: General partners of the private funds the organisation has committed to send capital call notices asking it to pay part of its unfunded commitment, usually with about ten business days' notice. Funds operations analysts retrieve each notice from a portal or mailbox, check the amount, balances and fees against the commitment record and fund terms, verify the payment instructions, book the call and set up the payment, which a second person reviews and, for large amounts, a director approves. The payment is released through the custodian on the due date, the liquidity team is told in advance, and Finance posts the accounting entries. Notices come in many formats and portals, discrepancies need back-and-forth with administrators, and changed bank details carry fraud risk, while missing a due date can trigger default remedies.

baseline.org_archetype: A national public pension investment manager of about 2,000 staff with C$44 to 54 billion of unfunded private fund commitments, whose 22-person funds operations team pays calls through a global custodian.
baseline.notes: Common practice of large LPs in the period: portal downloads, spreadsheet validation, a private investments administration system, custodian web platform and SWIFT, maker-checker approval.

trigger: A general partner or its administrator issues a capital call notice to the organisation's investing entity.
end_state: The call is paid on the due date, booked and posted to the accounting records, or a fraudulent notice is blocked.

volume.seasonality: Peaks near quarter ends, when GPs call fees and repay subscription lines, and in December.

evidence.note: Matches the organisation file's 190 to 340 notices a month, part of about 460 call and distribution notices from about 800 fund and co-investment interests; anchored on C$44 to 54 billion of unfunded commitments and about 170 PE managers plus real asset and credit funds.

Funds Operations handles capital calls (job posting); FTE share estimated from step times at 260 notices a month. Job Bank NOC 11100 Toronto median C$41.34 an hour before loading. Loaded cost from the organisation file (total compensation times a layer uplift calibrated to F2022 personnel expense, times overhead 1.25, over 1,950 paid hours).

Reviews bookings, calls back on changed instructions and releases payments; share estimated from step times plus exception handling. Loaded cost from the organisation file (total compensation times a layer uplift calibrated to F2022 personnel expense, times overhead 1.25, over 1,950 paid hours).

Approves payments above the senior's authority, about a third of calls at about 10 minutes each. Loaded cost from the organisation file (total compensation times a layer uplift calibrated to F2022 personnel expense, times overhead 1.25, over 1,950 paid hours).

Confirms the purpose of large, first or unusual calls for about a fifth of notices. Loaded cost from the organisation file (total compensation times a layer uplift calibrated to F2022 personnel expense, times overhead 1.25, over 1,950 paid hours).

Reviews and posts accounting entries generated from the private admin system, about 10 minutes a notice. Loaded cost from the organisation file (total compensation times a layer uplift calibrated to F2022 personnel expense, times overhead 1.25, over 1,950 paid hours).

systems.name: General partner and fund administrator investor portals
Document management and investment committee memo repository
Private investments administration and cash flow system
Global custodian web portal and statements
SWIFT messaging to custodians and banks
SimCorp Dimension investment book of record (portfolio accounting, treasury, performance)

steps.name: Retrieve notice from GP portal or mailbox
steps.description: An analyst sees a capital call alert in the shared funds operations mailbox, logs into the general partner's or administrator's investor portal with two-factor authentication, and downloads the notice and any cover letter. Portals differ for almost every manager, and some notices still arrive only as email attachments.

error.defect_description: Notice saved under the wrong fund interest or a duplicate notice downloaded twice.

evidence.note: Most managers use third-party administrators with their own portals (65% in 2018); retrieval time is an estimate.

steps.name: Log notice in capital call tracker
steps.description: The analyst records the fund, investing entity, notice date, due date, currency and amount in the team's capital call tracker so that every open call and its deadline is visible to the team and to Treasury.

error.defect_description: Due date or currency typed wrongly in the tracker.

evidence.note: Tracker logging is common practice for LP operations teams handling hundreds of notices a month; estimate.

steps.name: Match notice to fund interest and commitment
steps.description: The analyst opens the fund interest in the private investments administration system and pulls the commitment, the investing subsidiary, prior contributions and distributions, recallable amounts and the fee terms from the agreement and side letter.

error.defect_description: Notice matched to the wrong parallel vehicle or feeder entity.

evidence.note: ILPA notices carry fund name, LP name and ID and LP commitment, which the LP matches to its own records.

steps.name: Validate contribution and balances
steps.description: The analyst recomputes the organisation's share of the call from its percentage of commitments, checks that unfunded commitment, cumulative contributions and cumulative distributions before the notice agree with its own records, and that the call does not exceed the remaining commitment or the investment period limits.

error.defect_description: A beginning-balance difference is accepted without explanation.

control.basis: Investment Operations procedure: validate every capital call against commitment records before payment

evidence.note: ILPA template sections B and C give LP unfunded commitment and cumulative balances before and after the notice, and section D a variance to the prior notice, so the LP can reconcile them.

steps.name: Recompute fees and expenses in the call
steps.description: For calls that include management fees, fund expenses or interest on a subscription line, the analyst recomputes the fee on the agreed basis, applies offsets and side letter discounts, and checks expense categories against the partnership agreement.

error.defect_description: Fee offset or side letter discount not applied and not noticed.

control.basis: Fee validation against LPA and side letter terms

evidence.note: ILPA asks GPs to show management fee calculations, offsets and cumulative balances in each notice; the discrepancy rate is an estimate.

steps.name: Query GP or administrator
steps.description: The analyst emails the general partner's investor relations or the fund administrator with the specific difference, such as a fee offset not applied, a balance that does not match the last notice or a missing breakdown, and asks for an explanation or corrected notice.

evidence.note: ILPA guidance aims to minimise follow-up questions, which LPs raise when notices lack detail.

steps.name: Wait for GP explanation or revised notice
steps.description: The administrator answers or reissues the notice. Small differences are often explained without a change; others lead to a corrected notice that must be validated again before the due date.

evidence.note: Estimate of administrator response times inside a 10-business-day notice window.

steps.name: Check payment instructions against standing record
steps.description: The analyst compares the bank, account number, beneficiary and reference in the notice with the verified standing instructions held for the fund. Calls that are large, first calls, or name an unexpected investment are routed to the deal team.

error.defect_description: A changed account number is overlooked.

control.basis: Payment fraud controls: instructions must match a verified standing record

evidence.note: Spoofed capital call notices with changed bank details are a known fraud (Sequoia case); verified vendor or payee records are a standard control. Branch shares are estimates.

steps.name: Call back GP to verify changed instructions
steps.description: A senior associate calls the general partner's finance contact on the phone number already on file, never one in the notice, to confirm the new account, obtains signed confirmation, and has a second person approve the change to the standing record before any payment.

control.basis: Call-back to a known, previously validated number and dual approval of payee changes (funds transfer fraud prevention)

evidence.note: First Citizens guidance: call back on a known number and never use contact information in the request; dual authorisation of instruction changes. Share of fraudulent requests is an estimate.

steps.name: Deal team confirms purpose of the call
steps.description: The investment associate who follows the fund confirms that the investment named in the notice is one the general partner discussed, that the amount is consistent with the deal size, and flags any concern, such as a call for a deal the fund should be excused from.

evidence.note: ILPA cover letters for purchases name the company, deal parameters and use of capital, which the deal team can check; the routing rule is an estimate.

steps.name: Book call and create payment instruction
steps.description: The analyst books the contribution in the private admin system split by investment, fees, expenses and amounts inside or outside the commitment, and creates a payment instruction in the custodian platform for the due date from the investing subsidiary's account.

error.defect_description: Wrong amount, value date or transaction type keyed; payment and booking re-keyed in two systems.

evidence.note: Job posting describes system set-ups, transaction entries and settlements by the funds operations team; split by transaction type follows the ILPA template.

steps.name: Add call to cash forecast and fund the account
steps.description: The analyst adds the amount, currency and value date to the daily cash forecast sent to the liquidity team and, if the investing subsidiary lacks cash in that currency, asks Treasury to fund the account or buy the currency before the due date.

error.defect_description: Forecast omits the call or uses the wrong currency, leaving the account short on the due date.

evidence.note: The 10-day Liquidity Coverage Ratio measures liquid assets against obligations over any 10 days; ILPA asks GPs for quarterly call projections that feed forecasting.

steps.name: Review booking and payment as checker
steps.description: A senior associate who did not prepare the entry compares the booking and the payment instruction with the notice, the validation workpaper and the verified bank details, then approves both in the systems or returns them.

control.basis: Maker-checker review of transactions and payments; no single person initiates, approves and records

evidence.note: Segregation of initiating, approving and recording; authority split and return rate are estimates.

steps.name: Director approves large payment
steps.description: The director of private investment operations reviews the approval package for payments above the senior's limit, checks the call against the commitment and any deal team comment, and approves in the custodian platform.

control.basis: Payment authority limits under Management Authorities

evidence.note: Authority threshold and share above it are estimates.

steps.name: Release payment for value date
steps.description: On the business day before or on the due date a second authorised user releases the approved payment in the custodian platform, which sends it as a SWIFT payment instruction for same-day value. Payments are timed to the due date to keep cash invested.

error.defect_description: Payment released for the wrong value date.

control.basis: Dual authorisation in the custodian platform: releaser differs from initiator

evidence.note: With at least 10 business days of notice, most of the elapsed time is waiting for the due date; dual authorisation follows funds transfer fraud guidance. Wait range is an estimate.

steps.name: Custodian executes the wire
steps.description: The custodian debits the investing subsidiary's account and sends the wire to the fund's bank. A small share fail or return, for example because of intermediary bank details, insufficient cash or sanctions screening holds.

evidence.note: Failure rate is an estimate.

steps.name: Confirm settlement and close the call
steps.description: The analyst checks the custodian statement for the debit, settles the pending transaction in the private admin system, saves the confirmation and any GP receipt acknowledgement, and closes the tracker line.

error.defect_description: Settled amount not matched to the booking, leaving a cash break.

evidence.note: Daily reconciliation of outgoing payments is recommended practice; timing is an estimate.

steps.name: Investigate failed or returned wire
steps.description: A senior associate works with the custodian and the general partner to find why the wire failed, corrects the routing or funds the account, and re-sends the same day where possible, telling the general partner if payment will be late.

evidence.note: Mayer Brown: defaulting LPs owe punitive interest and face overcall, cram-down, forced sale and loss of voting rights, so failed wires are fixed urgently.

steps.name: Review and post accounting entries
steps.description: A fund accounting associate reviews the journal entries generated from the private admin system into the investment book of record, checks the cash and investment cost entries against the settled transaction, and posts them for the daily accounting close.

error.defect_description: Fees booked as investment cost or the wrong currency rate applied.

control.basis: Internal control over financial reporting: review of investment accounting entries

evidence.note: Step follows the organisation file's interface from capital calls to investment accounting; times are estimates.

exceptions.name: Discrepancy with the GP
exceptions.description: Balances, fees or the breakdown do not agree with the organisation's records; the analyst queries the administrator and re-validates the answer or a corrected notice.

exceptions.name: Changed payment instructions
exceptions.description: The notice shows new bank details; a senior associate calls back on the known number and a second person approves the change before payment. A few turn out to be spoofed notices and are blocked.

exceptions.name: Large or unusual call
exceptions.description: The deal team confirms the investment and amount, and payments above the senior's limit go to the director.

exceptions.name: Failed wire
exceptions.description: The custodian rejects or the bank returns the payment; operations fix the cause and re-send to avoid default interest.

exceptions.name: Short notice or netted call
exceptions.description: Some calls give fewer than ten business days or are netted against a distribution in the same notice, which compresses the review or adds a distribution split to the validation.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from notice retrieval to payment booked in the accounting records
benchmarks.population: Institutional LPs paying private fund capital calls on the due date

evidence.note: Derived: ILPA recommends at least 10 business days (about 14 calendar days) to respond, LPs pay on the due date, and entries post a day later.

benchmarks.population: Private equity funds following ILPA Principles

evidence.note: ILPA Principles 3.0: a reasonable window of at least 10 business days for LPs to respond to capital call requests.

pain_points.description: Notices arrive through dozens of different portals and formats, so retrieval and keying take time and errors creep in when the same data is typed into the tracker, the admin system and the custodian platform.

evidence.note: ILPA template exists to reduce LP processing errors and times; most managers use separate administrators.

pain_points.description: Fee and balance checks depend on reading partnership agreements and side letters, and differences take days of email with administrators inside a short notice window.

evidence.note: ILPA asks for fee calculations and offsets because LPs otherwise make follow-up inquiries.

pain_points.description: Spoofed notices with changed bank details are a real fraud risk, and the call-back and second approval add delay to a minority of calls.

evidence.note: Sequoia phishing case; funds transfer fraud guidance.

sources.title: Capital Call & Distribution Notice Best Practices, Version 1.1 (revised September 2016)
sources.supports: Notice content: LP and fund unfunded commitment and cumulative contributions and distributions before and after the notice, itemised investments, management fee calculations and offsets, due date, currency and FX, detailed payment instructions, beginning balance variance to the prior notice; purpose of reducing LP processing errors and times.

sources.title: ILPA Principles 3.0
sources.supports: LPs should have a window of at least 10 business days to respond to capital call requests; GPs should give quarterly projections of calls and distributions; disclosure of subscription credit facilities.

sources.title: Sequoia says phishing scheme tried to get LP to wire money
sources.supports: A spoofed email copying a real capital call notice asked an LP to wire a capital call to a bank account in Mexico; business email compromise risk in capital calls.

sources.title: Funds transfer fraud prevention
sources.publisher: First Citizens Bank Fund Banking (formerly SVB Private Funds CFO Insights)
sources.supports: Call back on a known, previously validated phone number and never use contact details in the requesting message; dual authorisation of changes to payment instructions; no single person should initiate, approve and record transactions; daily reconciliation.

sources.title: Understanding LPA default remedies
sources.supports: Remedies against an LP that fails to fund a call: default interest at a punitive rate, overcalls on other LPs, capital account cram-downs of 50 to 100%, forced sale at discounts such as 50%, withheld distributions, suspended voting and side letter rights.

sources.title: 2024 Private Investment Operational DDQ Analysis
sources.supports: 65% of private fund managers used a third-party administrator in 2018 and 83% in 2024; most funds rely on a single bank for capital calls and distributions.

assumptions: Distribution notices are handled in io-distributions; netted call-and-distribution notices are treated here as calls.
Most elapsed time is a deliberate calendar wait until the due date (s15), because payments are timed to keep cash invested; review work is done in the first two or three days.
Payment authority thresholds, branch shares, discrepancy and failure rates and all hands-on times are tier C estimates.
